boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Dalton II record (August 14-15, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. Wheeler's wider raid, the block-house surrender between Dalton and Tilton, Graysville and the pursuit into East Tennessee are context. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the District of Etowah and Wheeler's cavalry without counts; the live field reads zero. Steedman says his relief force was 1,800 effective, that he readied rail transport for 2,000 men, that Wheeler's command was not less than 6,000 in detachments of 1,000 to 3,000, and that the force attacking Dalton numbered about 3,000. NPS says the garrison was greatly outnumbered. The garrison's own strength is not given in the selected passage.
claims.rationale: Steedman's relief-force figure and his opinions of the enemy's size; none is a matched count and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result is a Union victory (the Confederates withdrew); the live page reads Union Victory. Steedman says he cleared the town at daylight; Cox says Wheeler was repulsed. NPS calls the engagement inconclusive but a Union victory because the Confederates withdrew.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 0 (US 0; CS 0). Steedman gives his loss as 1 officer and 8 men killed, 1 officer and 29 men wounded and 1 officer and 23 men missing, total 63; says the enemy left 33 dead and 57 badly wounded and lost not less than 200; and records the surrender of a block-house detachment of the Seventeenth Iowa between Dalton and Tilton.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The block-house surrender is a separate loss and is not added. The live zeros are not measured absence.

open_questions: Laiboldt's report, the Fourteenth U.S. Colored Infantry and other subordinate reports (Scearce's closing lines were read), Wheeler's raid report and Hood's report (families for other records) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Steedman's September 11, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 2, is a third family (interested Union account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
